audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows contradicted their own why-text and the packet chart.
audit.why: whys[0] says Level 1 is free damage for Riven but the row said Skill; whys[1] says 'both sides play patient' but the row said Riven; whys[2] gives Jax 'the clear trade advantage' but the row said Riven; whys[4] says every extended duel tilts his way but the row said Skill; whys[5] says 'genuinely 50-50' and whys[6] says keep trades short, but both rows said Riven. The mirror flipped exactly rows 0, 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Riven / Skill / Jax / Skill / Jax / Skill / Skill as matched full/content pairs in one group, with Level 1 to 7/10 and the two Jax rows to 4/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 why described Jax's ultimate with no cooldown at all.
audit.why: The active is 110 seconds at rank 1 — it is not something he throws into every trade, so knowing the number tells the player which fights are actually against the buffed version.
audit.corrected: whys[4] now carries the 110-second cooldown and keeps the three-second rule that follows from his stacking attack speed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page states in whys[2] and wants.foe[0] that Counter Strike's dodge 'absorbs Q autos and the stun interrupts Ki Burst', implying his E blanks Riven's abilities.
audit.why: Riot's text says Counter Strike lets Jax dodge all incoming ATTACKS — basic attacks. Riven's Broken Wings casts, her Q3 knockback and Ki Burst are spells and go through it untouched. What the dodge actually costs her is the Runic Blade auto-weave, which is where most of her damage sits. The distinction changes the play: a player who believes her stun is blanked will refuse to commit at all, when the correct line is to commit the casts and simply not spend autos into the dodge window. The mirror corrected the identical error from Jax's side.
audit.corrected: whys[2], spikes[1], wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0] all reworded so the dodge eats autos and the CC lands regardless.
sources: enemyKit E text 'dodge all incoming attacks'

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is the tracked cooldown on every screen of the entry with no number anywhere.
audit.why: It is 17 seconds at rank 1 and only reaches 9 at rank 5 — early on, a baited Counter Strike is a genuinely long window, which is why 'bait E and out-combo him early' is the win condition at all.
audit.corrected: whys[3] now gives 17s at rank 1 and states what the bait actually buys.

edits.before: His full kit lands: Counter Strike dodges Q autos and the stun interrupts Ki Burst, giving him the clear trade advantage.
edits.after: His full kit lands: Counter Strike dodges autos, not Ki Burst or Q3 — but it eats your Runic Blade weave, and that is the trade.

edits.before: Neither kit fully dominates — track Counter Strike's cooldown and only commit the full Q-W pattern when it is down.
edits.after: Neither kit dominates — Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1, so a baited E buys you a whole rotation — commit inside it.

edits.before: Grandmaster's Might stats are permanently active, the R active grants bonus armor and MR, and every extended duel from here tilts his way.
edits.after: His R stats sit on permanently and the active adds armour and MR on a 110s cooldown — every duel past three seconds tilts his way.

edits.before: Jax's full kit goes live and Counter Strike now threatens your entire Q-chain, flipping the trade advantage in his favour.
edits.after: Jax's full kit goes live: Counter Strike eats the autos inside your Q-chain and stuns after, flipping the trade to him.

edits.before: Land W-stun before Jax activates Counter Strike so his dodge window never covers your combo
edits.after: Ki Burst lands through Counter Strike — the cost of trading into it is your autos, so hold the weave

edits.before: Activate Counter Strike the instant Riven steps up, letting the dodge absorb Q autos and the stun interrupt Ki Burst
edits.after: Activate Counter Strike as Riven steps up so the dodge eats her empowered autos and the stun still lands after

notes: NAME CONFLICT I did not resolve: this brief's packet lists Jax's R as 'Grandmaster-at-Arms', but the page (and the already-published mirror, which explicitly validated it) calls it 'Grandmaster's Might'. The kit file is meant to be the authority on names, but overruling a mirror that checked the same field would put the two pages in disagreement, so I rewrote whys[4] without using the name at all. Raised in questionsForUser. The packet's suspectName ('Counter Strike's') is a FALSE POSITIVE — correct Riot name. The dodge-blanks-her-spells error also survives in the 'early' and 'mid' paragraphs ('his stun will interrupt Ki Burst mid-cast', 'stun you out of W'); both are long strings sitting among mojibake-carrying full-layer text, so they want the byte-exact pass. spikes[3] recommends Jax build 'Stride Breaker', which is not a current item name (Stridebreaker) — enemy build text, low stakes, left alone.
